OpenAI is launching a ChatGPT version for teenagers. The company describes this new initiative as "an experience designed to help young people learn, think critically, deepen their understanding, and confidently use artificial intelligence." The teen version of ChatGPT will activate when OpenAI's system estimates the user's age to be between 13 and 17, or when users directly declare their age.

OpenAI highlights four features launching alongside ChatGPT for teens:

  • Study Mode, which helps young people understand material through guided questioning and step-by-step support.
  • New responsible homework prompts that can recognise when teens are trying to take shortcuts to complete assignments and guide them to Study Mode for a step-by-step collaborative problem-solving process.
  • Quizzes and study visualisation features that give young people more ways to practise, let them test what they've learned, and present difficult concepts more clearly to check comprehension.
  • In addition, new Study Hours allow teens or parents to schedule times when Study Mode automatically turns on, making it easier to build good study habits into daily life.

ChatGPT for teens also includes the following safety and safeguards:

For teenage users, safety features are built in as part of the default experience. For users under 18, ChatGPT for teens will apply age-appropriate protections designed to reduce exposure to content that may be harmful or unsuitable for their developmental stage, while preserving the ability to learn, create, and explore. [...] This work also builds on our earlier family tools, including parental controls and notifications. Parents who have linked their teen's account can set quiet hours, manage specific settings, and receive safety notifications in limited high-risk situations. We are adding notifications related to eating disorders, while limiting the scope of information sharing and focusing on moments where offline support matters most.

OpenAI also detailed how ChatGPT works for users under 18, including the following healthy-use measures:

  • Sensitive image upload prompts, encouraging teens not to share private or sensitive images.
  • A teen-specific onboarding guide that introduces the available learning and safety features from the start.
  • Simple personalisation options, such as theme colours and voice variations, that help make the experience more personal without blurring the line between a useful tool and a relationship.
